fact_label: Territorial tax system — foreign-sourced income exempt
notes: Guatemala runs a territorial tax system — only Guatemala-sourced income is taxed; foreign-sourced income (remote client work, pension, investment income from abroad) is exempt from Guatemalan income tax. Tax residency triggers at 183+ days/year; once a tax resident, the practical step is an annual declaration flagging the foreign-source portion as exempt, process overhead rather than a tax bill. This is the load-bearing fact behind the Income viability (AI/remote fit) criterion's 4/5 score at both Antigua and Atitlán, extracted for the first time — the criterion was previously scored with zero backing fact rows in this file despite real, well-sourced reasoning already sitting in visa-legal.md's prose

value_raw: Documented proof of the qualifying investment, verifiable and shown to have arrived from abroad by bank transfer. Most commonly real estate: a notarized public deed (escritura pública) registered in the national property registry (Registro General de la Propiedad) — unregistered property does not count, and multiple properly-documented properties can be combined to reach the bar. Business capital, an earmarked bank deposit, or purchase of an existing business also qualify. Processing includes a mandatory field-verification step in which an inspector from Guatemala's immigration authority (IGM) confirms the investment and the applicant's address actually exist; realistic notarial/legal assistance costs sit on top of the official fees.
notes: Extracted 2026-08-06 ([specialist], verdict-coverage review) from the held record only — zero new research; the field-verification and registered-deed requirements are the 2026-07-09 re-verification pass's own findings. Informational by design — never a mechanical gate.
